Team — forwarding Acme's request. Quick internal sync notes and a proposed first-pass (see attached).

Assumptions I used in the draft:
- Model family: Llama2-13B (redwood-13b-q4) quantized 4-bit for embeddings and chat. We recommended a single-model strategy to simplify caching.
- Embedding batch sizes: 128 typical for embeddings; chat batch size: 8 (low-latency).
- Target steady throughput: 10k tokens/sec aggregate across pool (mixed traffic).
- Latency SLOs: chat p95 <= 350ms, p50 <= 100ms.
- Warm cache requirement: pre-warm KV for top-100 prompt prefixes; cold-start acceptable up to 2s for first token if model pinned.

Initial recommended capacity (conservative):
- 4 x H100 (or equivalent) for the low-latency lane (dedicated for chat), with 1-2 reserve nodes for burst.
- 2 x A10G for batch embeddings (cost-optimized).
- 100GbE RDMA between nodes, NVMe local scratch for cache.

Autoscaling policy (proposal):
- Scale-out at 65-70% GPU token throughput utilization.
- Cooldown: 3 minutes after scale-out event before scale-in.
- Canary warm-up: allocate 1 warm replica (pre-warmed KV cache) before adding to LB; 60s warm-up expected.

Please review numbers — Dev/Marissa can you run sims and real-ops estimates? Sanjay, if you prefer we can target H100-only pool instead of hybrid.

Adding technical detail from perf lab and estimation notes. High level: numbers below are back-of-envelope but grounded in our microbenchmarks for rdw-13b-q4.

Per-GPU throughput (single model, mixed batch sizes):
- H100 (1x): ~1,200 tokens/sec (steady-state, batching across requests, 4-bit quantized).
- A10G (1x): ~420 tokens/sec (optimized for batch embeddings).

Implications for Acme target (10k tokens/sec):
- H100-only: ~9 H100s to sustain 10k tokens/sec at 80% headroom; but with lane separation we recommended 4 H100s dedicated for chat and additional H100s for burst/throughput, or 4 H100 + 4 A10G hybrid to trade cost.
- Embedding lane (batchable): 2x A10G with batched embedding jobs (B=128) will handle current projection with room to spare.

Latency notes:
- With pinned/warmer KV cache and 100GbE RDMA, we see p95 for chat at ~220-300ms on H100s for B=8. Cold-start (first request to a scaled-up replica) is typically 800ms–2.2s depending on model load; we mitigate with pre-warmed replicas and short-lived standby instances.

Networking/storage:
- Recommend 100GbE RoCE/RDMA for cross-node KV fetch and model shard sync; 25GbE commonly causes higher p95 variance under load.
- Local NVMe for token KV/cache and model shard read cache; NFS introduces jitter.

Autoscaling & orchestration:
- Fast scale-out: use immediate allocation but mark new nodes as "warming" and do not route production traffic until HEAT (health + small synthetic load) passes (approx 45–90s).
- Cache pre-warm hooks: allow customer to upload hot prefixes or run a synthetic warm pass during maintenance window.

Edge cases / assumptions:
- All numbers assume 4-bit quant (q4) profile and our current kernel set. fp16 or unquantized models will increase memory needs and reduce per-GPU throughput by ~30–60%.

Happy to produce a slim table for procurement that maps node counts to expected p95/p50.

— Dev
Perf & Serving Engineering, Redwood Inference
